messages.author: bd6d05f06437885c
messages.subject: transformed Gaussian model with R-INLA
parts:
Hi all,
 
I recently read some literatures saying that some spatial geostatistical data often display non-Gaussianity, positive data, etc and suggesting that taking Box-cox transformation to the data and assume the transformed data to be Gaussian field. 
I wanna ask whether and how can I include such transformation in the spde model using INLA, and then get the proper prediction and sampling of the response variables? 
 
Thanks a lot!
 
Cheers,
David

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] transformed Gaussian model with R-INLA
parts:
Thanks! I checked the doc for Gaussian likelihood and found the link functions can be identity, logit, log. log seems ok for me but there is no box-cox transformation. 
I wonder if I can do the transformation first? For example the data are y.. and I generate a new data set y_new = log(y) , and then apply the ordinary Gaussian likelihood spde model to y_new.. is that the same as the inference using inla with link "log"? 
Many thanks !
